## Product safety news

### [Cotton On pays penalties for alleged product safety reporting breaches]

Cotton On Australia Pty Ltd (Cotton On) has paid penalties totalling $19,800 after the ACCC issued it with two infringement notices for failing to comply with mandatory product safety reporting requirements on two occasions. 

### [H&M pays penalties over absent and inaccurate fire safety warnings on kids' nightwear]

Fashion retailer H&M Hennes & Mauritz Pty Ltd (H&M Australia) has paid $138,600 in penalties for allegedly selling more than 4,000 items of children’s clothing without complying with the required fire hazard warning label requirements in breach of the Australian Consumer Law.

### [Kmart in court over safety concerns with cosmetic nail glue and button battery products]

The ACCC has commenced Federal Court action against Kmart Australia Ltd, a subsidiary of Wesfarmers (ASX: WES), alleging it breached the Australian Consumer Law by selling millions of units of cosmetic nail glue without adequate warnings and thousands of units of button battery products which did not comply with mandatory standards.

## How the ACCC protects consumers

### [About us]

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) is an independent Commonwealth statutory authority.

In product safety, our role is to address the risk of serious injury, serious illness and death from safety hazards in consumer products.

### [See what issues we're targeting]

Each year, we identify key priorities.We target the highest priority risks from unsafe consumer goods.

We raise public awareness and work to create the rules to protect consumers from unsafe products.

### [Product safety as a consumer guarantee]

Consumers have the right to expect certain things when they buy a product or service.

In consumer law, these basic rights are called consumer guarantees. One of these rights is products sold to consumers must be of acceptable quality and be safe.
